title: Choosing a Statistical Test — A Simple Map for Therapists

hook.en: The scariest part of a thesis for many therapists is "which test do I use?". The answer is not memory, it is three questions: what kind of outcome, how many groups, and are they independent? Answer those and the test almost picks itself.
hook.ur: Bohat se therapists ke liye thesis ka sab se daravna hissa hai "kaun sa test istemal karun?". Jawab yaadasht nahi, teen sawal hain: nateeja kis qism ka, kitne groups, aur kya woh azaad hain? In ka jawab dein to test khud-ba-khud chun jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll classify an outcome (continuous, ordinal, categorical), choose between a parametric and a non-parametric test, pick the right test for two groups, three or more groups, paired data, categories and relationships, and know free software to run them.
goal.ur: End tak aap nateeje ki qism (mustaqil, ordinal, categorical) tay karenge, parametric aur non-parametric test mein se chunenge, do groups, teen ya zyada groups, paired data, categories aur rishton ke liye sahi test chunenge, aur unhein chalane ke liye muft software jaanenge.

text.en: Start with the **type of outcome**: **continuous** (such as degrees, seconds, kilograms), **ordinal** (ranked, such as a 0 to 10 pain scale or Likert scale) or **categorical** (counts of categories, such as improved or not). Then ask **how many groups** and whether the observations are **independent** (different people) or **paired** (the same people measured twice). If a continuous outcome is roughly bell-shaped, use **parametric** tests (t-test, ANOVA); if it is skewed, ordinal or the sample is very small, use **non-parametric** tests (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis).
text.ur: **Nateeje ki qism** se shuru karein: **continuous** (jaise degree, seconds, kilogram), **ordinal** (tarteeb wala, jaise 0 se 10 dard scale ya Likert scale) ya **categorical** (categories ki ginti, jaise behtar hua ya nahi). Phir poochhein **kitne groups** hain aur kya observations **azaad** (mukhtalif log) hain ya **paired** (wohi log do baar naape gaye). Agar continuous nateeja taqreeban ghanta-numa ho to **parametric** tests (t-test, ANOVA); agar ek taraf jhuka hua, ordinal ho ya sample bohat chhota ho to **non-parametric** tests (Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis).

text.en: Think of **choosing a vehicle**. A bicycle, a car and a truck are all good, but you choose by the load, the distance and the road. A statistical test is the same: the data type, the number of groups and the design are the road and the load. The wrong vehicle can still move, but not well.
text.ur: **Gaari chunna** sochein. Cycle, car aur truck sab achhi hain, lekin aap bojh, fasle aur sadak se chunte hain. Statistical test bhi aisa hai: data ki qism, groups ka shumar aur design sadak aur bojh hain. Ghalat gaari phir bhi chal sakti hai, lekin achhi nahi.

question.en: You compare knee range of motion (in degrees, roughly bell-shaped) between two different groups of patients. Which test fits?
question.ur: Aap do mukhtalif mareezon ke groups ke beech ghutne ki range of motion (degree mein, taqreeban ghanta-numa) ka muqabla karte hain. Kaun sa test fit hai?

feedback.en: The outcome is not a category count.
Yes — a continuous, roughly normal outcome in two independent groups.
feedback.ur: Haan — do azaad groups mein continuous, taqreeban normal nateeja.

feedback.en: The groups are different people, not the same people twice.
feedback.ur: Groups mukhtalif log hain, wohi log do baar nahi.

question.en: The same 20 patients rate pain (0 to 10) before and after a programme, and the ratings are skewed. Which test fits?
question.ur: Wohi 20 mareez programme se pehle aur baad dard (0 se 10) rate karte hain, aur ratings ek taraf jhuki hain. Kaun sa test fit hai?

feedback.en: The data are paired, not independent.
That is for two independent groups.
feedback.ur: Yeh do azaad groups ke liye hai.

feedback.en: Yes — paired, ordinal or skewed data.
feedback.ur: Haan — paired, ordinal ya ek taraf jhuka data.

question.en: You want to know whether the proportion who return to work (yes or no) differs between two treatment groups. Which test fits?
question.ur: Aap jaanna chahte hain ke kaam par wapas aane walon ka hissa (haan ya nahi) do ilaaj ke groups mein mukhtalif hai ya nahi. Kaun sa test fit hai?

feedback.en: That compares means of a continuous outcome.
feedback.ur: Yeh continuous nateeje ke means ka muqabla karta hai.
Yeh do continuous naapon ko jorta hai.

text.en: Chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test if counts are small
text.ur: Chi-square test, ya Fisher's exact test agar ginti chhoti ho

text.en: **Picking the test after seeing which one gives p below 0.05.** Choose the test in your plan before looking at results. Another trap is using many t-tests when comparing three or more groups, which inflates false positives; use ANOVA (or its non-parametric partner) first. Also, a test only answers "is there a difference?". Report the effect size and confidence interval too, and do not use "not normal" as an excuse to skip checking the plot.
text.ur: **Test dekh kar chunna ke kaun sa p 0.05 se neeche deta hai.** Nateeje dekhne se pehle apne plan mein test chunein. Ek aur jaal teen ya zyada groups ke muqabale mein bohat se t-tests istemal karna hai, jo jhoote positive barhata hai; pehle ANOVA (ya uska non-parametric saathi) istemal karein. Test sirf "kya farq hai?" ka jawab deta hai. Effect size aur confidence interval bhi report karein, aur "normal nahi" ko plot dekhne se bachne ka bahana na banayein.

text.en: **Plot first, test second.** Draw the data as dots or a box plot before choosing a test. It shows skew, outliers and sample size at a glance, and it often answers the clinical question before any test. Free software such as jamovi or JASP lets you run the common tests with menus, and R is free for those who like code.
text.ur: **Pehle plot, phir test.** Test chunne se pehle data ko dots ya box plot ki shakal mein banayein. Yeh ek nazar mein ek taraf jhukao, outliers aur sample size dikhata hai, aur aksar kisi test se pehle clinical sawal ka jawab de deta hai. jamovi ya JASP jaise muft software menus se aam tests chalane dete hain, aur R un ke liye muft hai jo code pasand karte hain.

question.en: Do I need to test whether data are "normal" before every t-test?
question.ur: Kya har t-test se pehle data ke "normal" hone ka test zaroori hai?

answer.en: Not necessarily. Normality tests are unreliable in very small samples (where they lack power) and too sensitive in very large ones. It is usually better to look at a plot and to consider the sample size: t-tests are quite robust to mild non-normality when groups are of similar size and not tiny. When in doubt, a non-parametric test or a bootstrap is a safe backup.
answer.ur: Zaroori nahi. Normality tests bohat chhote samples mein na-qabil-e-aitbaar (power ki kami) aur bohat bade mein zyada hassas hote hain. Aam taur par plot dekhna aur sample size par ghaur karna behtar hai: jab groups ka size milta-julta ho aur bohat chhota na ho to t-tests halke non-normality ke liye kaafi mazboot hain. Shak ho to non-parametric test ya bootstrap mehfooz mutabadil hai.

beats.patient: A student has a 0-to-10 pain score for three groups: exercise, manual therapy and usual care, each with 20 different patients. Scores are clearly skewed.
beats.assessment: Three independent groups, ordinal or skewed data, so a non-parametric test for three groups.
beats.treatment: She uses the Kruskal-Wallis test, follows it with pairwise tests adjusted for multiple comparisons, and reports median differences with intervals and a box plot.
beats.reassess: The result is clear, honest and reproducible, and a reviewer can follow every step.

text.en: **Statistics cannot rescue a poor design.** The test does not fix bias, missing data or a poorly measured outcome. Before running any test, check that the design and data collection are sound. Do not "tune" the analysis until it works, and keep a record of every analysis you run.
text.ur: **Shumariyat kharab design ko nahi bacha sakti.** Test bias, ghayab data ya ghalat naapa gaya nateeja theek nahi karta. Koi test chalane se pehle dekhein ke design aur data jama karna durust hain. Analysis ko tab tak "tune" na karein jab tak kaam na kare, aur har chalaye gaye analysis ka record rakhein.

text.en: Standard medical statistics texts, such as Altman's Practical Statistics for Medical Research, set out the choice of test according to the type of data, the number of groups and whether samples are independent or paired, and caution that non-parametric tests are an alternative when assumptions are not met. Field's textbook explains the same logic with examples for software users and stresses plotting and checking assumptions before interpreting p-values.
text.ur: Altman ki Practical Statistics for Medical Research jaisi mayaari medical statistics ki kitabein test ka intikhab data ki qism, groups ke shumar aur samples ke azaad ya paired hone ke mutabiq batati hain, aur khabardar karti hain ke assumptions poore na hon to non-parametric tests mutabadil hain. Field ki kitab wohi mantiq software istemal karne walon ke liye misalon ke saath samjhati hai aur p-values ki tafseer se pehle plot karne aur assumptions jaanchne par zor deti hai.

text.en: **Type, Groups, Pairing.** Type of outcome, number of groups, and whether the observations are paired. Then check the shape.
text.ur: **Qism, Groups, Jorna.** Nateeje ki qism, groups ka shumar, aur kya observations paired hain. Phir shakal dekhein.

summary.en: Choose a test from three questions: outcome type, number of groups, and independent or paired data.
summary.ur: Teen sawalon se test chunein: nateeje ki qism, groups ka shumar, aur azaad ya paired data.

summary.en: Use parametric tests for roughly normal continuous data and non-parametric tests for skewed, ordinal or very small samples.
summary.ur: Taqreeban normal continuous data ke liye parametric aur ek taraf jhuke, ordinal ya bohat chhote samples ke liye non-parametric tests istemal karein.

summary.en: Plot first, plan the test in advance and report effect sizes with intervals.
summary.ur: Pehle plot karein, test pehle se plan karein aur effect sizes intervals ke saath report karein.
